podcast.title: Quitting Red Hot Chili Peppers (1988)
podcast.body: Jack Irons, the drummer for the Red Hot Chili Peppers, quit the band following the death of guitarist Hillel Slovak from a heroin overdose in June 1988, stating he "couldn't take it anymore." His departure left Flea and Anthony Kiedis to decide the band's future. "drummer Jack Irons couldn't take it anymore, so he quit, leaving just flea and anthony to do something, or not."

xref.title: Fandom and Joining Red Hot Chili Peppers (1984-1988)
xref.body: At 15, around 1984 when the Red Hot Chili Peppers released their debut album, John Frusciante became a dedicated fan, attending their shows and hoping to speak with guitarist Hillel Slovak. He learned all of their songs. Following Slovak's death in June 1988, and Jack Irons' subsequent departure, Frusciante, then 17, began attracting attention for his guitar skills. He turned down an offer from Frank Zappa due to Zappa's anti-drug stance, briefly joined L.A. punk band Thelonius Monster, but ultimately joined the Chili Peppers in October 1988, after a jam session with Flea. "Legend says that he was three hours into his membership with him, when the Chili Peppers called and said, okay, you got the gig. This was October 1988."

xref.title: Brief Red Hot Chili Peppers Drummer (1988)
xref.body: D.H. Peligro was briefly hired as the new drummer for the Red Hot Chili Peppers in 1988 after Jack Irons quit. He was a friend of John Frusciante and connected him to the band, but ultimately "didn't work out" as the drummer. "D.H. Polegrum, the dead Kennedays, was briefly hired as a new drummer... But he didn't work out."

xref.title: Death from Heroin Overdose (June 25, 1988)
xref.body: Hillel Slovak, the guitarist for the Red Hot Chili Peppers, died of a heroin overdose on June 25, 1988, while the band was working on a new album. His death led to drummer Jack Irons quitting the band due to his inability to cope. "But then Hilarl died of a heroin overdose on June 25, 1988, as the band was working on a new album."

xref.title: Early Formation of the Classic Lineup (1988-1989)
xref.body: Following the death of Hillel Slovak and the departure of Jack Irons in June 1988, the band auditioned Dwayne "Blackbird" McKnight, but he didn't work out. John Frusciante joined as guitarist in October 1988, followed by Chad Smith as drummer in December 1988. By early 1989, this new lineup of Frusciante, Smith, Flea, and Anthony Kiedis formed what would become known as the classic Red Hot Chili Peppers configuration, debuting on the album "Mother's Milk." "By the start of 1989, the Chili Peppers had undergone a complete refurbishment. John was the new guitarist and Chad was the new drummer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Formation Origin - Pickup Basketball Game (1989)
xref.body: The band's genesis began in Seattle when Stone Gossard and Jeff Ament formed Love Company and sought a singer by circulating a demo. Jack Irons, a former Red Hot Chili Peppers drummer, received a copy of this demo and passed it to Eddie Vedder, a surfer and night shift worker at a Chevron tank farm in San Diego, after a pickup basketball game in 1989. Eddie then wrote lyrics to three of the demo's five songs, dubbed them onto a new cassette, and sent it to Seattle, leading to his invitation to jam with the group and the formation of Pearl Jam. "This cassette passed out of a gym bag sometime in 1989 might have resulted in the most profitable pickup basketball game ever played."

xref.title: Bipolar Disorder
xref.body: A significant factor in Scott Weiland's and Mary Forsberg's struggles was their undiagnosed bipolar disorder, which led to extreme mood swings and poor judgment, often exacerbated by self-medication with drugs like crack. Doctors initially misdiagnosed him with severe depression, and the treatments did not control his manic episodes. "A big part of their problems coping with life is that they were both undiagnosed sufferers of bipolar disorder, and this is a really important part of our story."

xref.title: Early Formation and Friendship
xref.body: Hillel Slovak met Anthony Kiedis, Flea, and original drummer Jack Irons at Fairfax High School in Los Angeles, and by 1983, they were all playing together, forming the core of the Red Hot Chili Peppers. "He was born in Israel, and eventually ended up going to Fairfax High School in Los Angeles, where he met Anthony Ketus, Flea, and original peppers drummer Jack Irons."

xref.title: Eddie Vedder's Audition Tape Creation
xref.body: After receiving a demo tape from Jack Irons, Eddie Vedder listened to it repeatedly. Following a night shift and a surfing session, he sat down at home and wrote lyrics for three of the five songs on the tape. He then recorded his vocals and the new lyrics onto a cassette and mailed it to Seattle, where Jeff Ament and Stone Gossard immediately recognized his talent, solidifying his role as their frontman. "As soon as Eddie got the tape from Jack, he started listening to it over and over."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Formed from Anthem – Early Origins
xref.body: The Red Hot Chili Peppers were formed by Flea and Hillel Slovak after their previous band, Anthem, broke up. Jack Irons, another musician connected to the Seattle scene through Eleven and Pearl Jam, later joined the Red Hot Chili Peppers for a period. "One was named Flea, and the other was Hillel Slovak, and when Anthem broke up, those two guys would form the Red Hot Chili Peppers."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Jack Irons' Collaboration – During Matt Cameron's Soundgarden Tenure
xref.body: Jack Irons, who was once a drummer for Eleven and briefly for the Red Hot Chili Peppers, worked with Pearl Jam at a time when Matt Cameron was performing with Soundgarden. Irons also played a crucial role in Eddie Vedder joining the band by passing along a demo tape. "Jack would later join the Red Hot Chili Peppers for a bit, and he worked with Pearl Jam when Matt Cameron went off with Soundgarden."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Jack Irons' Drumming Role – Early Member
xref.body: Jack Irons, who later joined the Red Hot Chili Peppers and worked with Pearl Jam, was a drummer for Eleven at one point. His connections to the Seattle music scene further highlight the interconnectedness of many of the era's bands. "There Elaine and a friend named Natasha Schneider formed a group called Eleven, which at one point had a drummer named Jack Irons."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: The Wallflowers' Consistency
xref.body: Jacob Dylan has been the sole consistent member of The Wallflowers throughout its existence, a band that remains active today. The lineup has seen several changes, with notable past members including Jack Irons, formerly of the Red Hot Chili Peppers and Pearl Jam, and Rami Jaffee, keyboardist for Foo Fighters. "Jacob has been the only consistent member of The Wallflowers over all these years, which by the way is still a going concern. People to cycle through the band have included former chili peppers and pro jam drummer Jack Irons and Foo Fighters keyboardist Rami Jaffee."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
